ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Korea FIU designated list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List and country/regime programs, EU/UK HMT lists, and the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs' financial sanctions list for every shareholder (direct/indirect), director, officer, UBO and authorized representative. This includes negative news, PEP status within 12 months, source of wealth/funds for enhanced due diligence, ongoing monitoring, risk scoring for 'medium risk enhanced', and 7-year retention of all screening evidence. Domestic PEPs, foreign PEPs, family members and close associates require senior compliance approval and documented source-of-wealth verification before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (I-Registration)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company registry accepts only a Hangul-based registered name; a foreign-language-only name cannot be registered. A stock corporation must end with the Korean legal-form indicator 'Chusik Hoesa' at the tail end of the registered name. English or Revised Romanization transliterations may be filed only as auxiliary reference names in parentheses. The four-tier naming review is: (i) distinctiveness against identical or confusingly similar registered names; (ii) non-confusion with existing trademarks and business names; (iii) absence of prohibited, misleading, or state-sovereign tokens; and (iv) mandatory Korean legal-form suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation is automatically renewable for one additional 6-month period if an extension application is submitted in the I-Registration system before expiry. If the registry rejects a proposed name, an electronic rejection notice is issued. Within 14 days of receipt, the applicant may file a written Request for Reconsideration with the registry head under Articles 11 and 13 of the Administrative Procedures Act, attaching a legal opinion, evidence of distinctiveness, and, if applicable, prior ministerial approval for sensitive tokens. If reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal to the applicable Administrative Appeals Commission must be filed within 90 days of notice; the appeal does not extend the reservation deadline, so a parallel new name reservation should be opened immediately to preserve the commercial timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a VPN and network-privacy SaaS company under ISIC 6201, a pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or post office box is operationally rejected by the National Tax Service and Korean commercial banks. The Court Registry may initially accept a serviced-office address, but the NTS requires an actual physical business premise with a visible corporate sign, dedicated local telephone line, lease contract in the company's name, and supporting evidence of business activity before issuing tax registration and valid e-tax invoices. Korean banks will not open a corporate account for Stripe or Paymentwall payouts unless a physical site inspection is successfully completed. The minimum acceptable arrangement is a licensed serviced office with private meeting rooms, continuous access, and a registered operational desk; a pure virtual mailing address is never permissible for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for surprise inspection: (i) physical signage; (ii) lease agreement in the company's name; (iii) employee attendance and payroll records; (iv) server or cloud-infrastructure documentation; (v) network security subscriptions; (vi) books and records including e-tax invoices; (vii) corporate seals and resolution books. Quantified risk: 20-30% in the first operating year for a serviced office, 8-12% for a dedicated leased office, and up to 50-60% if the company files zero revenue while processing overseas Stripe/Paymentwall receipts. The NTS and the municipal gu tax office may conduct unannounced site visits without prior notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), particularly Articles 288 through 328 (incorporation, articles of incorporation, capital, shares, and promoters), Article 289 (articles of incorporation execution), Article 292 (registration of incorporation), Articles 312-316 (subscription and payment of shares), Article 317 (registration of incorporation), and Article 363 (first general meeting provisions). Furthermore, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA), Articles 2, 4, 5, and 6, governs foreign-invested stock corporations and the required Foreign Investment Report.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea (대법원 등기국) through the local Korean Commercial Registry Court (상업등기소) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; administrative online filings are processed via the Korean Supreme Court 'I-RO' (Internet Registry Office) system. For foreign investment-related notifications and tax incentives, the competent authority is the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Invest Korea and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation Registration (주식회사 설립등기신청서) together with the Articles of Incorporation (정관), and, for foreign investors, the Foreign Investment Report Certificate (외국인투자신고확인증) filed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Commercial Act of South Korea imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa; however, the Act requires that the total issue price of subscribed shares be paid in full no later than six months after the closing date of subscription, and prohibits payment by set-off in kind unless approved by the court-appointed inspector where required. For a foreign-invested company, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act requires a Foreign Investment Report to be filed before the share subscription; a remittance of the consideration must be made through a foreign exchange bank, and a deposit or escrow receipt issued by the bank must be attached to the registration application. The paid-up capital may be set at KRW 100 million (approximately USD 75,000) as a practical bank account and licensing threshold, but no blocked escrow account is legally mandated by the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Directors shall cause the issuance of share certificates and effect the registration of shareholders in the Company's register of shareholders, and shall take all necessary steps to maintain the full paid-up capital as a legal capital reserve in accordance with Articles 451 through 460 of the Commercial Act. 2. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Promoter Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public of the Seoul District Court or any Korean notary; subsequent filing through the Korean Supreme Court I-RO (Internet Registry Office).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (정관) in Korean, complying with mandatory content listed under Article 289 of the Commercial Act, including the corporate purpose, trade name, total number of authorized shares, par value and class of shares, registered office address, method of public notice, and the names of incorporating promoters. All promoters must sign and seal the articles. If the company will use an online filing system, each promoter and initial officer must obtain a Certificate of Seal Impression and provide a power of attorney authenticated according to the Registry Office practice. The articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public in the presence of all promoters or their authorized representatives.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Promoter identification documents (national ID or Alien Registration Card)
Power of attorney if any promoter is represented
Certificate of corporate seal or individual seal impression
Consent-to-use letter for registered office address
Statement of shareholder class and par value
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry office issues a correction order, the promoters shall revise and re-notarize the articles within 3 business days, paying any supplementary revenue stamp fees and resubmitting through I-RO; no new expedited application is required unless the corporate purpose materially changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Report and Capital Remittance Escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Invest Korea or a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a foreign investor, file a Foreign Investment Report under FIPA Article 4 before the subscription of shares, either online via the Invest Korea portal or by visiting a designated branch of a foreign exchange bank. The report must include the investor's name, nationality, amount and type of investment, and the intended business scope of the Chusik Hoesa. Upon approval or automatic processing, the foreign exchange bank issues a Foreign Investment Report Certificate and receives the purchase price for the newly issued shares. Non-resident investors must remit the subscription proceeds in foreign currency or KRW through a designated foreign exchange bank and obtain a deposit receipt or proof of remittance that will be attached to the incorporation registration. The capital must be kept in a Korean corporate bank account after incorporation, but no blocked escrow account is legally required by the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Report Form
Certificate of Incorporation or passport of foreign investor
Power of attorney appointing a local agent
Foreign exchange bank deposit receipt of share payment
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of corporate seal of the Korean local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign exchange bank or KOTRA queries the investment purpose or source of funds, the investor must submit a certified bank statement or source-of-wealth declaration within 5 business days; if the Foreign Investment Report is rejected, the application may be resubmitted after correcting the business scope or investor details through the same window without penalty, unless the rejection is based on a prohibited sector.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment Registration Filing with the Commercial Registry Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office through the local Commercial Registry Court located in the judicial district of the registered office; online filing via I-RO.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 2 weeks of the date of subscription closing, the promoters or the appointed Representative Director must file the Establishment Registration application under Article 317 of the Commercial Act. The application must be submitted in Korean through I-RO, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the written subscription document, receipts evidencing full payment of the share price, the minutes or written resolution of the first board meeting if conducted before registration, the report of the inspector where in-kind contributions exist, the consent letter of the registered office owner, and a certified power of attorney. If the paid-up capital is fully paid and all statutory officers have accepted appointment, the court registrar examines the filing for legal compliance, verifies the registered office, and enters the corporation into the commercial registry. A legal registration seal may be issued after the public announcement.
required_dossiers: Application for commercial registration (establishment)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscription statement and share payment receipts
Report of inspector for in-kind contribution, if any
Consent-to-use and landlord's certificate for registered office
List of directors, representative director, and auditor with acceptances of office
Foreign Investment Report Certificate and foreign exchange bank deposit receipt
Certificate of corporate seal and specimen of corporate seal
Power of attorney for filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a suspension (보정명령), the applicant must submit the missing or corrected documents through I-RO within 2 weeks; failure to cure results in withdrawal of the application and a new filing fee. If the entry is rejected due to defective articles, the promoters must convene to amend the articles and re-file, and any interest or penalties are limited to the registry fee re-payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registration, Social Insurance Enrollment, and Corporate Seal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax; local district tax office; National Health Insurance Service; Korea Workers' Compensation; Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) for seal registration if desired.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after the commercial registry entry, the Representative Director must file the corporate incorporation tax report under the Corporate Tax Act Article 109, apply for a business registration certificate (사업자등록증) from the competent district tax office, and obtain a tax invoice and digital certificate for HomeTax. The company must also enroll as an employer with the National Health Insurance Service and the Korea Workers' Compensation and Employment Insurance Service if it has or plans to hire employees, even if initially only directors. The corporate seal should be registered with the registry court to allow officers to issue certificates and execute contracts; a corporate online banking resolution is then filed with the company's bank. Any Value-Added Tax registration is required if the entity will supply goods or services in Korea.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate
Certificate of corporate seal
Application for business registration (사업자등록신청서)
Articles of Incorporation and corporate bank account statement
Identification and Alien Registration Card of the Representative Director
Copy of lease agreement or registered office title
Foreign Investment Report Certificate if foreign-invested
Power of attorney for tax accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the district tax office defers the business registration for non-foreign investment reporting or incomplete lease evidence, the applicant must cure the missing documents within 7 business days; reinstatement is automatic after the lease certificate is received. If the tax office issues a refusal for prohibited activity, the entity may file an administrative appeal with the National Tax Service within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - this entity is a pure digital/online Virtual Private Network (VPN) network privacy application provider classified under ISIC 6201 (Computer programming activities) and NAICS 517919 (All Other Telecommunications). It does not operate physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facilities (ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - No industrial manufacturing permit or physical operating license is required for a software-as-a-service entity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Environment of South Korea and Korea Environment Corporation have no jurisdiction because the VPN network privacy app business does not generate point-source discharges, emissions, or hazardous waste requiring EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Full EIA Report and Environmental Registration are not applicable for ISIC 6201 software businesses; no site discharge or waste derogation is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste handling thresholds apply. Only standard office waste and electronic waste recycling under the Waste Management Act apply, with e-waste disposal through a licensed electronics recycler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at site level: because the company does not operate a physical production facility, no Civil Defense fire safety certificate for industrial premises, structural load inspection, or workplace safety installation approval is required for manufacturing. However, the registered office must be a legally occupied business premises that satisfies ordinary building code fire safety requirements and maintains basic workplace safety compliance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act for any non-industrial office staff; no separate industrial fire permit is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS); online portal HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr), with Korea Customs Service under the Ministry of Economy and Finance operating the UNI-PASS export declaration system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A wholly domestic Chusik Hoesa must apply for a business registration number with the NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over its Korean place of business within 20 days from commencement of business. The application is made on the NTS business registration form, together with the articles of incorporation, corporate certificate of registration, three-year business plan or lease contract of the Korean registered office, and identification of the representative; NTS issues the 11-digit business registration number, which is simultaneously the corporate tax TIN and the VAT registration number. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean place of business that supplies VPN/network privacy app electronic services to Korean consumers, the foreign entity must appoint a Korean tax representative (Korean certified tax accountant or attorney) and file a simplified VAT registration application with the NTS if its Korean electronic-service turnover is expected to exceed the statutory threshold of KRW 30,000,000 per annual taxable period. The application must attach the foreign certificate of incorporation, board resolution, certificate of representative, power of attorney to the local tax representative, and the contract or platform evidence showing Korean-sourced electronic supplies; NTS then issues the same 11-digit business registration number for VAT filing and zero-rating compliance. Foreign shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa are not separately required to obtain Korean TINs unless they are engaged in their own Korean taxable business or have Korean-source taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide check-the-box elections or hybrid-mismatch transparency elections for Korean Chusik Hoesa corporations. A Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily taxed as a resident entity under the Corporate Tax Act and is not eligible for pass-through classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea, administered by the NTS; non-resident digital service suppliers are subjected to VAT through the simplified foreign operator VAT registration mechanism for electronic services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a domestic Chusik Hoesa there is no monetary turnover threshold: VAT registration is mandatory upon commencing any taxable business in Korea. For a non-resident foreign supplier of electronic services to Korean consumers, mandatory VAT registration is triggered when annual Korean electronic-service supplies exceed the statutory threshold under the Value-Added Tax Act and Presidential Decree, currently KRW 30,000,000; below that threshold registration is voluntary rather than mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a mandatory electronic tax invoice system under which every VAT-registered business must issue an e-tax invoice through the NTS HomeTax e-Tax invoice system or an NTS-approved service provider for taxable business-to-business supplies. The invoice data is submitted in near-real time via XML, API, or EDI interfaces and is centrally matched by the NTS against VAT returns, corporate tax returns, cash receipt and credit card sales data, and customs export declarations. There is no physical fiscal stamp or pre-approval clearance; the fiscal clearance and anti-fraud control is achieved through mandatory e-tax invoice transmission, sequential invoice validation, and administrative penalties for non-issuance or false e-tax invoice issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Korean VAT-registered business may export goods with a 0% VAT rate where the goods are shipped from Korea under a customs export declaration and consideration is earned in foreign currency from the foreign buyer. VPN/network privacy software-as-a-service and electronic digital content may be zero-rated as an overseas supply when the customer is a foreign non-resident recipient, the service is delivered and consumed outside Korea, and the subscription fee is received from abroad in foreign currency. The exporter must maintain evidence of conclusion of contract, service delivery, and actual inward foreign exchange remittance; only these verified supplies may be recorded as zero-rated rather than standard-rated supplies in the quarterly VAT return. Excess input VAT connected with zero-rated exports is refundable after NTS documentary verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration issued by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS (the Korean equivalent of the Bill of Entry/export declaration)
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill in the name of the foreign buyer; for digital/SaaS/VPN app supplies, an electronic delivery and usage record evidencing foreign subscriber consumption
Commercial invoice and signed contract / purchase order
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Certificate issued by a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank evidencing the foreign currency collection
Packing list, export insurance or other trade documents necessary to prove the physical export
NTS zero-rated export supporting schedule / export performance confirmation when requested during audit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS will compare zero-rated return claims with UNI-PASS customs declarations, e-tax invoice transmissions, and foreign exchange bank reports. If the required customs, delivery, contract, or foreign-currency remittance documentation is missing or inconsistent, or if export consideration is not repatriated within 180 days, the zero rating is denied with retrospective effect, the supply is reclassified as a standard-rated Korean supply, and 10% VAT is assessed, together with penalty taxes under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act. The exposure includes non-payment/under-reporting penalties of up to 40% of the unpaid VAT, false e-tax invoice penalties, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for fraudulent export zero-rating claims, plus statutory interest on all clawed-back amounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), acting as the central bank and foreign-exchange market supervisor, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; day-to-day transaction reporting is collected through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) operating via licensed foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized current-account regime. Payments for software subscriptions, license royalties, VPN access fees, and data-processing services are generally treated as invisible current transactions and may be remitted freely through licensed foreign exchange banks, provided the underlying purpose is truthfully disclosed and the remittance is reported where applicable. Capital-account transactions, by contrast, remain subject to a rule-based declaratory system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act: equity contributions, offshore loans, deposits, and guarantees require prior declaration, though not necessarily administrative approval, and any unauthorized cross-border capital flow may be investigated by MOEF and BOK. For a foreign-owned Korean Chusik Hoesa, inbound capital is additionally governed by the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA), which requires a foreign-investment notification and a foreign-investment registration certificate before the remittance is booked as share capital. Dividends, branch remittances, and liquidation proceeds are convertible only after corporate tax and withholding tax clearance; a bank will require a formal dividend resolution, audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, and evidence that the company is not delinquent on Korean statutory contributions. The Korean won is not an internationally delivered currency in the general sense; onshore settlement occurs in KRW, and export proceeds in foreign currency may be retained in designated foreign-exchange accounts or converted at market rates without a fixed mandatory surrender ratio. However, every transaction above the statutory reporting threshold must be transmitted to FEIS by the handling bank. Overall, convertibility is high for bona fide operating cash flows, but it is a documentary discipline rather than an unfettered freedom, and compliance failures can result in administrative penalties, retroactive tax reassessment, and deferred remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, export proceeds—including software licensing and VPN subscription revenue invoiced to non-residents—must be collected within six months from the shipment or service-provision date through a licensed foreign exchange bank. The invoiced proceeds must be credited to the exporter's foreign-currency account or sold to the bank; there is no fixed statutory conversion percentage imposed on the date of collection. Instead, the key legal requirement is timely collection, accurate reporting, and retention in a permitted account. Any conversion of retained foreign currency into KRW must be executed at prevailing market rates with a licensed bank, and the bank must file the transaction to FEIS. If proceeds are kept beyond the statutory collection period or remain unusually unused, the entity must submit an extension or explanation to the bank and, if required, to MOEF/BOK. For VPN services settled through Stripe or Paymentwall, the gateway settlement in USD or EUR is treated as service-export revenue and should be reconciled against the underlying merchant agreement, invoicing module, and subscriber data so that the bank can confirm the flow is trade-related rather than an unlicensed money transmission activity.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Direct offshore EMI viability is very low. An offshore digital EMI is not licensed in Korea under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act or the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and therefore cannot open resident KRW settlement accounts, cannot connect to the BOK interbank payment rails, and cannot act as a licensed cross-border FX intermediary for the Chusik Hoesa. Such entities may be legally barred from providing deposit-taking or payment-account services in Korea, and Korean commercial banks will generally reject an onboarding package that relies on an unlicensed EMI for inbound share capital, subscription revenue settlement, or dividend repatriation. Stripe and Paymentwall can be used only as merchant acquirers and collect-on-behalf-of platforms; the final clearing and FX conversion must land in a domestic Tier-1 bank account in the Korean entity's name. Attempts to route operational subscriptions through an unlicensed international wallet or EMI structure will trigger AML suspicion, foreign-exchange offense risk, and possible violation of Korea's real-name financial transaction framework. The treasury architecture should therefore treat Stripe and Paymentwall as front-end payment gateways only and anchor all primary liquidity in a licensed Korean bank.

stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa, the statutory representative director or a properly authorized delegate with a notarized and apostilled power of attorney must appear physically in-branch for account opening. Remote-only video onboarding is not generally sufficient because Korean financial institutions are bound by the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and require face-to-face verification of the director, passbook/seal registration, and beneficial owner identity documents. In practical terms, the representative director should travel to Seoul or Busan, present their passport and, if available, Alien Registration Card, complete the bank's AML questionnaire, and execute the corporate account agreement in person. Some banks permit consular or notarial proxy opening if the entity and shareholder are both already known to the bank and if the proxy letter explicitly authorizes the signatory to satisfy FEIS and AML declarations; however, this is exceptional and usually requires a compliance committee override. For a VPN and privacy software entity classified as Medium Risk Enhanced, the issuer treasury should plan for the ultimate beneficial owner to be available for a physical interview and follow-up KYC video call, plus a written representation on the nature of the encryption product, its data retention policy, and its compliance with Korean privacy regulation (PIPA) and the Information Security Management System certification regime.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting, approval of financial statements and dividend declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; minutes recorded in the company's statutory minute book and available for inspection by shareholders and, in litigation, by the Commercial Registration Court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after each fiscal year end; for a December 31 year-end, by March 31 of the following year, extendable by one month under Commercial Act Article 365 but not later than June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors failing to convene the Annual General Meeting face administrative fines of up to KRW 10,000,000 (approximately USD 7,400) under Commercial Act Article 635; financial statements not approved at the AGM cannot support legal dividends and any unlawful distribution must be returned to the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return with tax adjustment statement and financial statements attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year following the tax year for a December 31 fiscal year-end; for other fiscal year-ends, within 3 months of fiscal year end; a one-month extension is available on application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax; under-reporting triggers an additional 10% (and 40% for fraud); unpaid tax accrues daily late-payment interest of 0.025%. NTS may seize bank accounts and assets. Tax delinquency alone does not immediately strike off the company, but continued non-operation and non-registration for more than 5 years can lead to the registry court's ex officio dissolution order under Commercial Act Article 520-2.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surcharge return (local income tax on national corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the national corporate income tax return deadline; for a December 31 year-end, no later than April 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an additional 20% of the unpaid local income tax; unpaid local income tax accrues daily interest of 0.025% and the municipal tax authority may issue compulsory collection and seizure orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual Value Added Tax returns and payments for January-June and July-December periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half period: July 25 of the same calendar year; second half period: January 25 of the following year; if the date falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-filing imposes an additional 10% of the unpaid VAT; fraudulent under-reporting attracts a 40% additional tax; overdue VAT accrues daily interest of 0.025% and supports NTS attachment proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage and salary withholding tax settlement return and four-major social insurance wage adjustment declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service; National Pension Service; National Health Insurance Service; Korea Employment Information Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual withholding payroll tax return: March 10 of the following year; social insurance wage adjustment declarations: March 15 of the following year, or the next business day when the fixed date falls on a non-business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or under-declaration exposes the company to administrative fines, contribution arrears interest, and additional social insurance surcharges of up to 20% of unpaid premiums; continued nonpayment can result in criminal prosecution and asset seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent external audit report by registered certified public accountants, when the statutory audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service for auditor registration and designation; the audit report is presented to shareholders at the Annual General Meeting and attached to the National Tax Service corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the AGM, which must be held within 3 months (or 4 months with extension) of fiscal year end; for December year-end companies, the audited financial statements must accompany the March 31 corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If a mandatory audit is omitted, the financial statements are not effective for dividends, surplus distributions, or tax loss carry-forward purposes; responsible directors and auditors may face administrative sanctions and fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies of up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 37,000), plus designation revocation and regulator orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Enterprise business report, if the Chusik Hoesa is registered as a foreign-invested company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each fiscal year end and within 30 days after any change in the foreign investor, investment amount, shareholding ratio, or business scope
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false filing is punishable by administrative fine under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act of up to KRW 2,000,000 (approximately USD 1,500), cancellation or revocation of foreign-invested enterprise registration, and loss of tax and customs incentives attached to foreign investment status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Chusik Hoesa must appoint an independent external auditor when: (1) total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million); (2) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion (approximately USD 5.4 million) and annual revenue equals or exceeds KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.7 million); (3) the company is listed or subject to public offering disclosure; or (4) the Financial Services Commission designates the company for selective audit based on quantitative criteria including at least 100 full-time employees with total assets above KRW 7 billion. A full statutory audit must be performed by a Korean-registered CPA firm independent of management; companies below the threshold but above the 'audit review' designation set forth in the FSC Notice may be required to undergo a less extensive Korean Standards on Auditing review engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For statutory external audit and financial reporting, K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed companies and for designated audit-target companies; non-listed companies may use K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) or K-IFRS, and small and medium-sized enterprises below the mandatory audit threshold may use the Korea SME Accounting Standards. The corporate income tax return is prepared on a local GAAP basis with a tax-adjustment schedule reconciling accounting profit to taxable income under the Corporate Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public annual beneficial ownership registration return for private Chusik Hoesa companies. However, under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and the Specific Financial Information Act, the corporation must maintain accurate beneficial-ownership identification records and disclose them to financial institutions at account opening, upon any transaction that triggers customer due diligence, and at least annually during AML/CFT compliance reviews. Any share transfer that results in direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more of the shares or voting rights must be entered in the Register of Members within 30 days of the closing or payment date; for foreign-invested companies, the same change must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act within 30 days. Failure to update the register makes the transfer ineffective against the company and subjects the company and responsible directors to civil liability, administrative fines, and criminal penalties for false beneficial-ownership declarations of up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 37,000).

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,500 per annum for a standard registered office address, compliance mailing address, and resident corporate agent services in Seoul or Gyeonggi; higher if licensed corporate secretarial, bookkeeping, or payroll support is bundled
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 25,000 for a non-listed Chusik Hoesa statutory audit under K-GAAP; USD 25,000 - USD 60,000 if K-IFRS, consolidated financial statements, regulatory designation, or multi-entity audit scope applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (upper-band national rate; aggregate 26.4% including the 10% local income tax surcharge)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean statutory incentives include a progressive 9% rate on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income; R&D expense tax credits for high-tech and privacy-enhancing technology under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act; investment and employment tax credits; Free Economic Zone and foreign-invested high-technology company tax holidays/reductions; no separate patent-box regime, but R&D credits and deductions materially reduce the effective tax burden for a VPN/privacy SaaS company

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 1: Corporation Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement) and mandatory attachments filed electronically through the NTS HomeTax e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return with mandatory semi-annual interim prepayment returns
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final return is due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa the statutory deadline is 31 March. The interim prepayment for the first 6 months is due within 3 months after the end of the interim period, i.e., by 30 September for calendar-year companies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business registration number, corporate registration number, fiscal year, tax office, business code for ISIC 6201 / NAICS 517919, Korean domicile, foreign investment report number, and non-resident ownership declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every direct and indirect non-resident shareholder, foreign ownership percentage, and foreign director tax identification number. If a foreign investor holds 10% or more, input the Foreign Investment Promotion Act filing reference. Do not omit beneficial-ownership data of the ultimate foreign shareholder; incomplete non-resident data exposes the filing to withholding and treaty-claim rejection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Balance Sheet and Net Assets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assets, liabilities, capital stock, retained earnings, cumulative translation adjustments, and separately stated intangible assets for software, source code, user database, network infrastructure, and goodwill
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Software and source-code value must not be artificially stripped to a foreign affiliate. For an inbound non-resident enterprise with a Korean permanent establishment, only PE-attributable assets and liabilities are included; without a PE, foreign assets are excluded and only Korean-source items are relevant. For the Korean resident entity, worldwide assets are reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Income Statement and Reconciliation of Accounting Profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from VPN subscriptions, privacy-app licenses, digital network services, support and other operating income; cost of sales; gross profit; selling and administrative expenses; R&D expense; and accounting pre-tax income reconciled to taxable income through permanent and temporary differences
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Stripe/Paymentwall settlement amounts with bank deposits and processor statements. Cross-border charges to foreign affiliates must be characterized correctly as royalties, service fees, or intra-group tangible transactions. A resident Korean corporation files on worldwide income; a non-resident with a Korean PE files on business profits attributable to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax Base Computations and Deficit Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income, tax-exempt income, deductible reserves, prior-year tax-loss carryforwards, minimum tax adjustments, and the resulting taxable base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards are recognized for 10 years and are subject to strict book-tax persistence rules. A non-resident corporation claiming a Korean PE must attribute profit under the Korean arm's-length and PE rules; treaty-based profit attribution cannot move Korean-source VPN revenue out of the return unless the PE-dependency and function, asset, and risk allocation is factually established.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Corporate Income Tax Calculation and Progressive Rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory progressive rate brackets: KRW 0-200 million at 9%; KRW 200 million-2 billion at 19%; KRW 2 billion-300 billion at 21%; excess over KRW 300 billion at 24%; calculation of basic national corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a Korean PE apply the same progressive rate table to PE-attributable taxable income. Non-resident corporations without a Korean PE do not file this main return for Korean-source business income; their income is subject to final withholding or a special simplified return. Dividends paid abroad are not deductible in Box 5 but appear in the withholding schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Credits and Foreign Tax Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D credits, investment and employment tax credits, foreign tax credits on foreign-source income, disaster/restructuring credits, and final national corporate income tax after credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are allowed only for foreign-sourced income actually taxed abroad and only to the Korean taxpayer; credits earned by the Korean entity cannot offset the shareholder's dividend withholding tax. In cross-border VPN structures, NTS will scrutinize payments booked in overseas affiliates to determine whether they are disguised royalties or profit-shifting charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6+ - Local Income Tax, Withholding Schedules and Payment Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of national corporate income tax, interim tax prepayments, withheld taxes, penalties, and resulting final payment or refund; detailed schedule of non-resident dividends, interest, and royalties and treaty rates claimed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide a payee-level schedule for each foreign recipient showing tax residence, Tax Residency Certificate reference, beneficial ownership, and the specific treaty article for the reduced withholding rate. Dividends paid to non-resident shareholders are generally subject to 20% national withholding plus 2% local surcharge unless a valid DTA reduction is substantiated. Payments to zero- or low-tax jurisdictions require contemporaneous economic-substance evidence in the transfer-pricing attachment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an additional tax of 20% for non-filing; negligent underreporting attracts 10%; intentional omission or concealment may attract 40% additional tax; late payment additionally accrues a statutory daily surcharge, recently approximately 0.022% per day, until the deficiency is paid. Aggregate tax, interest, and surcharges can substantially exceed the original tax liability. Fraudulent filing gives rise to criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment and fines where the tax evaded exceeds statutory thresholds. Failure to file non-resident withholding schedules is independently penalized with additional taxes of 10%-30% and can trigger director personal liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national dividend withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge, aggregating to 22% for non-resident shareholders absent a tax treaty reduction; treaty rates generally range from 5% to 15% depending on the DTA and shareholding percentage
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before the dividend is paid, the Korean payer must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, a beneficial ownership statement, and if applicable evidence proving the required minimum shareholding period and compliance with the Limitation-on-Benefits or Principal Purpose Test. The payer files the NTS prescribed Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction Application form and submits it to the tax office with the withholding remittance. Treaty relief is denied if the recipient is a conduit resident in a no-substance jurisdiction or if the arrangement was undertaken mainly to obtain treaty benefits. Where a treaty claim is not made before payment, the taxpayer must later pursue a refund through a written correction, Tax Tribunal appeal, or responsible tax litigation, so contemporaneous documentation is mandatory.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Non-treaty royalties are subject to 20% national withholding plus 2% local surcharge, aggregating to 22%; non-treaty interest is likewise 20% plus 2%, aggregating to 22%. Treaty rates generally reduce royalties and interest to 10%-15% depending on the applicable Korea DTA. For a VPN/privacy SaaS business, character is critical: subscription access to software is often business income taxable only if attributable to a Korean PE, whereas technology and trademark royalties are Korean-source income subject to withholding; interest on intercompany debt can be recharacterized as disguised equity if the Korean entity is thinly capitalized or repayment terms are inconsistent with arm's-length behavior.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File are triggered when annual foreign related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 5 billion; consolidated multinational group revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more triggers a Country-by-Country Report; separate reporting and lower compliance thresholds apply to transactions with comprehensive tax-haven jurisdictions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime, but the National Tax Service applies a statutory substance-over-form doctrine and the arm's-length principle under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act. For a VPN/privacy-app Korean operating entity, core income-generating activities include server and network administration, encryption software development, user contracting, access provisioning, payment and AML compliance, and local decision-making. These Korean functions, assets, and risks must support the reported income. Paper-only boards, foreign-resident decision-makers, and uncontrolled foreign servers weaken the Korean CIGA-equivalent substance, create PE exposure for foreign counterparties, and trigger anti-abuse denial of DTA benefits or controlled foreign corporation reattribution for Korean shareholders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating worldwide revenue generated through Stripe/Paymentwall by directing VPN subscription or privacy-app payments to foreign bank accounts, issuing no tax invoices, omitting revenue from statutory books, or fabricating technical-support expenses paid to related entities that perform no genuine service
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3: imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to twice the evaded national tax; where evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million, aggravated imprisonment up to 10 years and a fine up to three times the tax evaded. The Basic National Tax Act imposes an additional tax of 20%-40% of the under-reported or unpaid tax and daily late-payment surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director is personally secondarily liable under Basic National Tax Act Article 39 when corporate assets are insufficient and the director willfully failed to pay tax; personal bank accounts and assets may be attached. The NTS may impose departure restriction and blacklisting orders under the National Tax Collection Act, and a criminal conviction results in imprisonment, fines, and prohibition from future corporate service.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Resident Withholding Tax Evasion and Improper DTA Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, interest, or royalties to foreign shareholders or affiliates without withholding the statutory 22% aggregate tax, applying a zero or reduced treaty rate without a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership substantiation, or mischaracterizing royalty income as tax-free business income despite the absence of a factual Korean permanent establishment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Law Articles 5, 73 and 76 impose additional withholding taxes of 10% for non-withholding, 20% for under-declaration, and up to 30% for failure to remit withheld amounts, plus daily late-payment surcharge; a retrospective audit can deny treaty reductions and claw back foreign-investment incentives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and withholding officers are jointly and severally liable for unremitted withholding tax and surcharges; personal assets can be seized without a separate veil-piercing determination where funds were diverted. Intentional non-withholding constitutes criminal tax fraud punishable by imprisonment and fines, and responsible non-resident directors are subject to travel bans and NTS blacklisting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Shell Company, Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Economic-Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Korean Chusik Hoesa solely as a paper shell with no employees, servers, board activity, local decision-making, or genuine VPN/network operations, while attributing most profits to a zero-tax foreign affiliate through inflated software license fees, artificial IP transfers, or cost-allocation schemes that lack commercial reality
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Adjustment of International Taxes Act Articles 4-6 and 12 authorize the NTS to re-determine income at arm's length, impute profit to the Korean entity, levy a 10% surcharge on the adjusted amount, and impose interest; anti-abuse rules under the Principal Purpose Test or Limitation-on-Benefits cancel treaty relief; CFC rules tax foreign undistributed profits in the hands of Korean shareholders; foreign-investment incentives may be revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced where the company is a facade and assets are stripped; directors face secondary tax liability under Basic National Tax Act Article 39, civil damages under Commercial Act Article 401, and criminal prosecution. If the artificial structure is used to launder funds through alternative payment rails or to operate unlawful VPN or data-privacy services, the director may be sentenced under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information to up to 5 years' imprisonment, criminal fines, forfeiture of digital and fiat assets, and travel ban/blacklisting.
